title: Matching hot-path iteration: incremental node chunks, direct price extrema and in-place partial fills
status: implemented and validated locally; not committed or pushed

architecture.transaction: Command-level isolated candidates and clearing-failure rollback retained. No undo-log replacement or relaxation of failure contracts.
architecture.nodes: Order ID -> compact slot handle in a persistent ordered index; large order nodes in persistent Vector chunks. FIFO links and price heads/tails use direct private slot handles. Freed slots are reused within each candidate version.
architecture.prices: Use ordered-map get_min/get_max instead of constructing a keys iterator for each best-price lookup.
architecture.partial_fill: Update remaining quantity and cached level total in place; preserve the existing FIFO links and account index instead of removing and reinserting the maker.
architecture.reduce_only: Skip the reduce-only scan when there are no protected orders. Earlier attribution of two allocations per fill to the empty set was incorrect; the isolated extrema probe identifies the nonempty price-tree iterator as their source.
architecture.checkpoint: Legacy queue/location JSON fields remain; slot handles and account indexes are derived on restore.
architecture.memory: Arena chunks/free list share immutable versions. Slots are reused, but the active arena retains capacity up to its historical peak slot count; checkpoint reconstruction compacts it. This is not a claim of bounded total memory because accepted order IDs and histories are also retained.
architecture.selection: A hash-trie of compact slot handles was also tested locally and was slower on the exploratory matrix; the final implementation keeps an ordered index.

correctness.differential_scope: 5 seeds, 16 accounts, limit/post-only/IOC/FOK/market/cancel/amend, duplicate/invalid IDs and quantities. Randomized stream uses Both position side and excludes reduce-only; existing core/server tests cover hedge/reduce-only/protection/liquidation.
correctness.new_regression: 128 slots, eight complete cancel/refill generations, partial-head FIFO, old live and empty candidates remain independent, slots reused without arena growth, serialize/restore and continue matching.

performance.method: Each matrix: legacy, stage1, current, current, stage1, legacy; three blocks per executable, median of six block medians per variant. All own tests/builds stopped during final measurements. Other work on this Windows host was not isolated; values are local microbenchmarks, not service SLO or production qualification.
performance.matching_scope: Release, two spot accounts, one price, unit makers, 1/100/1000 complete fills, sequential and permuted IDs; partial rows fill 1 of a 1000-unit head maker. Empty input event history. Shared raw resets clone the seed; unique raw resets independently deserialize it; both resets are excluded. Spot apply includes its internal candidate and clearing. All event/account assertions and state/result destruction excluded. 5 warmups, 20 samples, 3 blocks. Seed validated against ordinary apply at 16 makers. No server, journal, network or durable commit timing.
performance.matching_comparability: Shared reset excludes its clone: old queues are copied and unique, persistent versions still share nodes with the live seed. Unique reset independently deserializes each variant outside the timer; decoding also changes allocation/cache layout, so it is a distinct workload. Both are reported. Legacy raw has no equivalent command rollback; spot apply includes candidate/clearing/old-state drop. Assertions and result/state destruction excluded. Blocks alternate book sizes. IDs are sequential or a coprime permutation, avoiding a favorable key-locality-only conclusion.
performance.order_command_scope: Release local microbenchmark of current dirty checkout. One funded account, no fills, empty history, no server/journal/network. Seed setup and external reset excluded; apply's internal clone and old-state drop included. 10 warmups, 80 samples, 3 blocks; ascending/descending sizes. Raw operations use an externally cloned reset: legacy queues are unshared, persistent nodes share roots with the seed. Raw add is prepared by add/cancel outside the timer (spare queue capacity in the legacy build). Account release and engine apply measured with live originals sharing account tables, as transaction candidates do. Seed book/accounts and order events checked against ordinary apply at n=16, canonicalizing unordered HashSet serialization.

allocation_probe.method: Allocation counts only, System allocator, operation only, reset and destruction excluded; realloc counts full requested new size. No latency conclusions from this instrumented executable.
allocation_probe.warning: Requested allocation traffic includes the full requested new buffer size for realloc, not peak resident memory. Instrumented timings are not used for latency conclusions.

limits: Bulk raw matching still has overhead relative to the original mutable queue; stage2 improves it rather than eliminating it. Full spot transaction benefit and raw matching regression are separate findings.

Matching throughput is measured for one price and two accounts only; command-size scaling separately uses 1/100 levels and up to 100000 orders. No new throughput qualification for hedge/reduce-only/liquidation/perpetual scenarios.
Event/history growth, HTTP/WebSocket, scheduler contention, journal, PostgreSQL durable commit and crash recovery latency are excluded from these microbenchmarks.
Short sub-microsecond operations have coarse timer resolution and host noise; use absolute cost and block spread rather than precise multipliers.
Persistent chunks and index paths still incur copying/indirection. Matching an exchange-grade mutable arena plus explicit transaction log is outside this iteration.
